memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then the LORD said to Moses, 'Stretch out your hand over the sea so that the
waters may flow back over the Egyptians and their chariots and horsemen.' Moses
stretched out his hand over the sea, and at daybreak the sea went back to its
place. The Egyptians were fleeing toward it, and the LORD swept them into the
sea." - Ex 14:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The same hand that opened the sea now closes it. The same waters that were a
highway for Israel become judgment for Egypt.

We should not rush past the weight of this. An army drowned. These were men with
families waiting at home. Scripture reports it plainly and does not celebrate
their deaths with cruelty.

It is worth remembering what God says elsewhere about such moments: "I take no
pleasure in the death of anyone" (Ezek 18:32). God is not casual about this. And
Egypt had been given warning after warning, mercy after mercy, and had chosen
this pursuit with their eyes open, even after seeing the sea divided.

There is a further sobering note. Egypt had once drowned Hebrew infants in the
Nile (Ex 1:22). What Egypt had done to the helpless now came back upon its army.
God's justice is not random.

For us, the lesson is not gloating but reverence. The same event that saves one
person exposes another. The cross works this way too. It is either where our
judgment fell on Christ, or it is where we stand outside the shelter.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you hold God's mercy and His justice together, or only one of them?
2. Have you taken shelter in Christ, or are you still standing outside?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are merciful and You are just. Teach me to hold both with reverence,
and thank You that my judgment fell on Jesus. Amen.
